reasons: The claimed deviation is correct: p0076's fifteen-day conformance window plus the express sunset ('after that date Vendor has no correction or refund obligation') falls far short of the preferred 12-month/90-day position and neutralizes the Section 19.4 remedy, so an actionable edit is warranted.

The redline reaches the playbook position: it sets twelve months for Deliverables/delivered software and ninety days for Services conformance, deletes the sunset, and affirmatively preserves the existing Section 19.4 correction/replacement/refund remedy rather than duplicating it — directionally correct for the customer.

The failed 'minimal edit' check (ratio 0.658) is advisory and justified here: the sentence is short and both the period and the sunset clause had to be replaced, so a whole-sentence rewrite is the smallest edit that achieves the position; no unrelated terms were introduced.
Adding the ninety-day Services conformance and 'software delivered to Customer' language tracks the preferred position's express software/services split rather than expanding scope beyond the rule.

Comment is accurate and compliant with tone rules: correct [Playbook] prefix, first person plural, explains the two changes and why (the sunset gutted 19.4), cites the playbook position, and offers the 90-day/30-day fallback without lecturing.
